chunks: The (legislated) shares (of inheritance) do not increase/exceed, and they cannot be more than six.
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Umar ibn Udhayna — similar to that.

key_terms.السِّهَامُ: The legally designated shares of inheritance as specified in Quran 4:11-12, 4:176 — each heir receives a fixed fraction
key_terms.تَعُولُ: From 'awl' (عَوْل) — the contested jurisprudential doctrine of proportional reduction of inheritance shares when their total exceeds the estate; rejected in Shia law
key_terms.سِتَّةٍ: Six — the maximum number of distinct inheritance fractions: 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 2/3, 1/3, 1/6

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about the maximum number of inheritance shares in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes a fundamental principle of Islamic inheritance law: the designated shares (al-sihham) can never exceed six in total, and the phenomenon known as 'awl' (proportional reduction when shares exceed the estate) is invalid. This ruling directly challenges the Sunni jurisprudential doctrine of 'awl' adopted by Umar ibn al-Khattab, affirming instead the Shia position that shares are fixed and the excess goes to the closest surviving male relative (asaba). A second chain from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman through Umar ibn Udhayna transmits the same ruling, reinforcing its authority through multiple chains.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazal Bin Shazaan altogether from Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Muhammad Bin Muslim and Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar and Bureyd Al Ajaly and Zurara Bin Ayn, 
Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The (legislated) shares (of inheritances), there is no deficiency/excess (therein), and they cannot be more than six’.
And from him, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from Umar Bin Azina, - similar to that.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ’Udhaynah from Muhammad ibn Muslim and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar and Burayd al-‘Ijliy and Zurarah ibn ‘A‘yan who has narrated the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, The ordained shares do not face deficiency and they are not more than six.’”
It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from ‘Umar ibn ’Udhaynah a similar Hadith.
